title: Applied anatomy: the femoral triangle, femoral canal and femoral hernia, and femoral artery access

guidelineVersions: Seto et al., FAUST, JACC Cardiovasc Interv (2010)

related.why: The inguinal canal and inguinal hernia: the other half of groin anatomy

brief.scenario: Mrs Margaret Hollis, 76, has had a painful, tense, irreducible lump in her right groin since yesterday and has vomited twice. The examiner will ask you about the anatomy of her right groin.
brief.task: Answer the examiner's questions on the femoral triangle, the femoral canal and femoral arterial access, and relate them to her presentation.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Borders, contents lateral to medial, sheath, then the canal. Finish with where to puncture the artery.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Calling any groin lump an inguinal hernia. Find the pubic tubercle first.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "The femoral triangle: inguinal ligament above, sartorius laterally, adductor longus medially."

grid.label: Borders of the triangle
grid.fail: Puts sartorius medially, or cannot name the floor.
grid.pass: Inguinal ligament above, medial border of sartorius laterally, medial border of adductor longus medially. Roof fascia lata.
grid.high: Adds floor (iliopsoas, pectineus, adductor longus), the saphenous opening in the roof, and the apex leading into the adductor canal.

grid.label: Contents and sheath
grid.fail: Places the femoral nerve inside the sheath, or the vein lateral to the artery.
grid.pass: Lateral to medial: femoral nerve, artery, vein, canal. The sheath holds artery, vein and canal; the nerve lies outside it.
grid.high: Sheath is a funnel of transversalis and iliac fascia; the canal holds lymphatics and a deep inguinal node; the canal lets the vein expand.

grid.label: Femoral ring
grid.fail: Cannot name the borders of the femoral ring.
grid.pass: Anterior inguinal ligament, posterior pectineal ligament, medial lacunar ligament, lateral femoral vein.
grid.high: Three of the four borders are rigid; an abnormal obturator artery may cross the lacunar ligament and bleed if it is divided.

grid.label: Femoral or inguinal
grid.fail: Diagnoses an inguinal hernia without locating the pubic tubercle.
grid.pass: A femoral hernia lies below and lateral to the pubic tubercle; an inguinal hernia emerges above and medial to it.
grid.high: Adds that femoral hernias are often small, irreducible and missed in obese patients, and that saphena varix and lymph node are differentials.

grid.label: Acts on strangulation
grid.fail: Suggests elective listing or attempts forceful reduction.
grid.pass: Recognises likely strangulation from a narrow rigid neck: resuscitate, senior review and emergency repair, prepared to resect bowel.
grid.high: States femoral hernia is a risk factor for strangulation, and that even non-emergency femoral hernias need timely repair.

grid.label: Puncture landmarks
grid.fail: Would puncture above the inguinal ligament, or wherever the pulse is felt.
grid.pass: Common femoral artery at the midinguinal point, below the inguinal ligament and above the bifurcation, over the femoral head.
grid.high: Uses the inferior epigastric artery on angiography as the upper limit; the femoral head gives a firm surface to compress.

grid.label: Access complications and ultrasound
grid.fail: Cannot link puncture height to a complication.
grid.pass: High puncture: retroperitoneal haematoma that cannot be compressed. Low puncture: pseudoaneurysm or arteriovenous fistula. Uses ultrasound guidance.
grid.high: Cites FAUST: ultrasound improved first-pass success and reduced venepunctures and vascular complications.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: What are the borders of the femoral triangle?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: The inguinal ligament above, adductor longus laterally and sartorius medially.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: The femoral vein laterally, then the artery, with the nerve inside the femoral sheath.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'm not sure. It's just below the ligament.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Her lump is in the groin. What is it?

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: It's irreducible. What would you do?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Try to reduce it, then list her for repair.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Where would you puncture the femoral artery for angiography?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Wherever the pulse is strongest, above or below the ligament.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I don't think it matters much.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What are the borders of the femoral triangle?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Inguinal ligament above, medial border of sartorius laterally, medial border of adductor longus medially. The roof is fascia lata.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Lateral to medial: femoral nerve, artery, vein and the femoral canal. The sheath contains the artery, vein and canal; the nerve is outside it.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Inguinal ligament in front, pectineal ligament behind, lacunar ligament medially and the femoral vein laterally.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: How do you know her lump is femoral?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: It lies below and lateral to the pubic tubercle. An inguinal hernia emerges above and medial to it.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The neck is narrow and rigid, so this is likely strangulated. I'd resuscitate her, get senior review and arrange emergency repair, ready to resect bowel.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Where would you puncture the femoral artery?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The common femoral artery at the midinguinal point, below the inguinal ligament and above the bifurcation, over the femoral head.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What if you're too high or too low?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Too high risks a retroperitoneal haematoma you cannot compress. Too low risks pseudoaneurysm or arteriovenous fistula. I'd use ultrasound.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Inguinal ligament, sartorius and adductor longus. The floor is iliopsoas, pectineus and adductor longus. The saphenous opening is in the fascia lata roof, and the apex leads into the adductor canal.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: A funnel of transversalis fascia in front and iliac fascia behind. The canal is its medial compartment, holding lymphatics and a deep inguinal node, and giving the vein room to expand.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Why does a femoral hernia strangulate?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Three borders of the ring are rigid ligament. If I need to divide the lacunar ligament, an abnormal obturator artery may cross it and bleed.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Femoral hernias are often small and missed in obese patients. A saphena varix or a lymph node can look similar.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Femoral hernia is a risk factor for strangulation, so even a non-emergency femoral hernia needs timely repair.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: How do you confirm the puncture site?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: On angiography the lower border of the inferior epigastric artery marks the upper limit. Over the femoral head there is bone to compress against.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: In FAUST, ultrasound improved first-pass success and reduced venepunctures and vascular complications.

failures.move: Calling the lump inguinal without finding the pubic tubercle.
failures.consequence: Misses a femoral hernia, which carries a high strangulation risk.
Delays surgery for strangulated bowel, or reduces dead bowel into the abdomen.
Bleeding tracks into the retroperitoneum where it cannot be compressed.

failures.move: Placing the femoral nerve inside the sheath.
failures.consequence: Misunderstands the order used for femoral nerve block and arterial access.

recovery.when: You lose the order of contents
recovery.line: Lateral to medial: nerve, artery, vein, then the empty space of the canal.

recovery.when: Asked to distinguish a groin lump
recovery.line: I'd find the pubic tubercle first: femoral below and lateral, inguinal above and medial.

knowledge.fact: Femoral triangle: inguinal ligament, medial border of sartorius, medial border of adductor longus.
Lateral to medial: femoral nerve (outside sheath), artery, vein, canal.
Femoral ring: inguinal, pectineal and lacunar ligaments, and the femoral vein.
Femoral hernia: below and lateral to the pubic tubercle; a risk factor for strangulation; timely repair.
Puncture the common femoral artery over the femoral head, below the inferior epigastric artery.
Ultrasound guidance reduces attempts, venepunctures and vascular complications.

recall.think: Irreducible groin lump in an older woman: strangulated femoral hernia.
recall.say: "Below and lateral to the pubic tubercle: femoral hernia, likely strangulated."
do: Emergency repair, ready to resect bowel

numbers.meaning: first-pass femoral puncture success, ultrasound vs fluoroscopy (FAUST)

recall.trap: A small, irreducible lump in an obese patient is easily missed or called a node.
recall.finish: Emergency femoral hernia repair; for access, ultrasound-guided common femoral puncture over the femoral head.

partner.opening: Mrs Hollis has an irreducible lump in her right groin. Tell me the borders of the femoral triangle.

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks where the lump lies
reveals.finding: Tense, tender 3 cm lump below and lateral to the pubic tubercle; no cough impulse; irreducible.

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks about her general state
reveals.finding: Pulse 108, colicky abdominal pain, two vomits, not passed flatus today.

reveals.trigger: Candidate is asked how to confirm the puncture site
reveals.finding: Read out: a right femoral angiogram shows the main artery of the groin crossing the medial half of the femoral head. Just above the top of the femoral head, a branch leaves it and curves upwards and medially into the anterior abdominal wall; the lowest point of this branch's curve lies level with the top of the femoral head. Just below the lower margin of the femoral head, the artery divides into two.

push.question: What are the borders of the femoral triangle?
push.expect: Inguinal ligament, sartorius, adductor longus; roof fascia lata.

push.question: What lies in the femoral sheath?

In a prosection of the right femoral triangle, a structure lies immediately lateral to the femoral artery, outside the femoral sheath. What is it, and in what order do the other contents lie medial to it?
push.expect: Femoral nerve; then artery, vein and canal, lateral to medial; the sheath holds artery, vein and canal.

push.question: What forms the femoral ring?
push.expect: Inguinal, pectineal and lacunar ligaments; femoral vein.

push.question: In a diagram of the femoral ring, a curved, sharp-edged ligament forms its medial border, close to the pubic tubercle. What is it, and why does it matter when repairing a strangulated femoral hernia?
push.expect: Lacunar ligament; it is rigid, so the neck is narrow and strangulation likely; an abnormal obturator artery may cross it and bleed if it is divided.

push.question: Is this femoral or inguinal?
push.expect: Below and lateral to the pubic tubercle: femoral.

push.question: Where would you puncture the femoral artery?
push.expect: Common femoral artery over the femoral head, below the inguinal ligament.

push.question: What happens if you are too high or too low?
push.expect: Retroperitoneal haematoma; pseudoaneurysm or arteriovenous fistula.

curveballs.prompt: The lump is soft, has a cough thrill and disappears on lying down.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Consider a saphena varix; duplex ultrasound will confirm.

curveballs.prompt: After angiography she becomes hypotensive with back pain and no groin swelling.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Suspect retroperitoneal haematoma from a high puncture: resuscitate, CT and senior vascular review.

curveballs.prompt: A pulsatile groin mass appears two days after catheterisation.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Femoral pseudoaneurysm: confirm with duplex ultrasound and refer to vascular or interventional radiology.
